Marisol Vega

• 3rd+

Owner at Vega Roofing | Storm damage and roof replacement across Central Texas

Visit my website

1d

Hail season is here, and most roof claims we see start with damage nobody noticed.

Hi, I’m Marisol Vega and this is why.

After every storm we walk the roof, the gutters and the attic before writing anything.

Here is what we look for first:

1. Granules in the gutters, which means the shingles are wearing.

2. Dents on the soft metals: vents, flashing and the gutter itself. They tell you how big the hail was.

3. Soft spots in the decking near the valleys, where water sits longest and rot starts before you see a stain.

4. Lifted or creased shingles on the side that faced the wind.

5. Water stains on the attic sheathing, always.

None of these take more than an hour to check, and all of them matter.

Insurance adjusters see dozens of roofs a week. If you can show them photos of each one, the claim goes faster.

Homeowners: take photos of your roof every spring, before storms come.

Roofers: send your customers a short checklist after every job so they know what to watch for next season.

We put ours on the fridge magnet we leave behind, and it brings us more calls than any ad.

If you’re in Central Texas and not sure what you’re looking at, send me a photo and I’ll tell you.

No charge, no pressure, no sales pitch.

Stay safe out there this season, everyone.

Full checklist on our site: vegaroofing.example/checklist

    Priya Raman

    • 3rd+

    Kitchen and bath remodeler in Austin | 20 years of cabinets, tile and happy clients | Licensed and insured

    Book a consultation

    1d

    We finished this kitchen in Travis Heights last week.

    The owners had one request for us:

    Storage.

    So we moved the fridge, added a pantry wall and doubled the drawers.
    The old layout had three cabinets nobody could reach without a stool.

    Here’s what made the biggest difference:

    • Drawers instead of base cabinets
    • A pantry wall where the desk was
    • Outlets inside the cabinets for the coffee maker and toaster

    • Under-cabinet lights on their own switch, so nobody wakes the house at six
    • A tall cabinet by the door for brooms and mops

    The hardest part was not the build. It was getting the electrician, the plumber and the countertop crew in the same week without anyone waiting on anyone.

    Lesson:

    A shared calendar beats fifty texts, every single time.

    We now book every trade on one board.

    Nobody waits, nobody double-books, and the client sees it all.

    Questions about kitchens? Ask away.
    I answer every comment, usually within the same day.

    Before/after below.
    Swipe to see the old layout next to the new one we built.

    If you’re a contractor in Austin and want to swap notes on scheduling trades, my inbox is open.

    And if you’re a homeowner planning a remodel next year, start now: the good crews book out six months ahead.

    Huge thanks to the crew who made this one happen, and to the owners for trusting us with their home.

    More photos on our page.
    Have a good week.

    🏡

    Winter is coming early to Central Texas this year.

    Is your plumbing ready for it?
    Here’s our checklist for the first freeze:
    1. Insulate exposed pipes: guide riogrande.example/freeze
    here

    2. Disconnect garden hoses

    3. Know where your main shut-off is

    4. Drip faucets
    5. Insulate
    6. Caulk
    7. Heaters
    8. Relax
    Most frozen pipes we see could have been avoided.

    A frozen pipe can burst and flood a home in under an hour.

    If yours freezes, shut off the water at the main and call a licensed plumber right away.

    Our crews will be on call around the clock during every freeze this winter, with trucks in Austin, Round Rock, Georgetown and San Marcos so we can reach you fast.

    Stay warm, Texas.
    Call us anytime:
    512-555-0147 (24/7)
    Or book online today.

    And a special shout-out to our newest master plumber, who passed his exam this month after four years with us.

    We’re proud of you,

      Elena Ruiz

      • 2nd

      Solar sales lead at SolarBridge | Helping Texas homeowners cut their power bills

      Promoted by SolarBridge

      Last month I helped forty families in Hays County switch to solar, and every one of them asked the same question:

      Will it actually pay for itself? So I sat down with our installers and our finance team and put together the real numbers for a typical Texas home, with no sales gloss.

      Short answer: for most homes it does, usually in seven to nine years, sooner if you add a battery.

      SolarBridge has put the whole breakdown in an article, with the numbers for three real homes we finished this summer.

      What surprised me most was how much the roof matters. A roof that needs replacing in five years changes the math completely, so we now check every roof first.
      If you’re a roofer in Central Texas, I’d love to compare notes. Our customers keep asking who we trust for roof work before an install.

      If you’re a homeowner, send me your last two power bills and I’ll tell you honestly whether solar makes sense for your house. solarbridge.example/payback
